advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the ticket dir in `_first_in_progress_ns` via `resolve_ticket_dir_name` instead of joining the raw `ticket_id`, matching `latest_screen_tally`.
evidence: `resolve_ticket_dir_name` docstring (src/rebar/_ids.py:286-290): 'Read sites that build a filesystem path from a ticket id use this in place of the unsafe `resolve_ticket_id(id) or id` idiom'
The new `latest_screen_tally` in the same change DOES use it: completion_sidecar.py imports `from rebar._engine_support.resolver import resolve_ticket_dir_name` and joins `os.path.join(tracker, rid)`
advisory.finding: `_first_in_progress_ns` constructs the ticket directory path directly from the raw `ticket_id` (`os.path.join(tracker_dir, ticket_id)`) instead of resolving via `resolve_ticket_dir_name`, the safe idiom the rest of the codebase — including the sibling `latest_screen_tally` added in this same change — uses. When the passed id is not exactly the directory name (an alias/short id), `os.path.isdir` is False and the function returns None, silently falling back to the epic's `created_at` anchor (a wider window) rather than the true first-in_progress transition.
scenarios: `epic_bug_candidates` called (directly or transitively) with an alias/short id rather than the canonical dir-name id — the anchor silently widens to created_at instead of the true claim time.
advisory.suggested_fix: Resolve the directory name first (mirroring latest_screen_tally): `rid = resolve_ticket_dir_name(ticket_id, str(_config.tracker_dir(repo_root)))` inside a try that returns None on FileNotFoundError, then `ticket_dir = os.path.join(tracker, rid)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the overflow-only case (no A-verdicts), emit a note-only block or adjust the header/prose so it does not instruct the verifier to 'adjudicate each' non-existent candidate.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py:202: `if not surfaced and screen_overflow <= 0: return ""` — so overflow-only (surfaced empty, overflow>0) still emits the block

The emitted prose (candidate_block body): 'The screen below flagged open/in_progress bugs ... as candidate defects in the epic's own deliverable. Adjudicate each ...' is unconditional, yet no `- id — title` rows follow when `surfaced` is empty
advisory.finding: `candidate_block` emits the full header and the prose 'The screen below flagged open/in_progress bugs ... as candidate defects ... Adjudicate each' even when zero A-verdicts surfaced and only `screen_overflow > 0`. The block then lists no candidate rows — only the overflow NOTE — so the verifier is told to 'adjudicate each' against an empty candidate list.
scenarios: An epic close where every screened candidate returned B/C but the candidate count exceeded the ceiling: the verifier receives an 'adjudicate each' instruction with only an overflow note and no listed candidates.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a precheck test that forces epic_bug_floor_findings to raise and asserts the close proceeds (run_verify True, not floor-blocked) with certifiable=False.
evidence: gate_ops.py:84-106 — `try: floor = epic_bug_floor_findings(...) except Exception as exc: ... uncertified = list(uncertified) + [{...}]` — the read-error degrade-open-withhold-certification arm.
Commit message: 'a floor read error withholds certification instead of blocking or crashing, mirroring the child-closure read-error arm.'

search_files for `epic_bug_floor_findings` in tests: only direct-call tests (lines 79-129) and a non-epic guard patch (line 450, which asserts it is NEVER called for a task) — none monkeypatch it to raise inside completion_precheck.

The child-closure analog IS tested end-to-end: test_completion_verification_workflow.py:217-262 (test_child_enumeration_read_error_withholds_certification) forces list_tickets to raise and asserts certifiable=False; no epic-floor equivalent exists.
ABSENCE: no test asserts, after forcing the floor read to raise, that out['run_verify'] is True, the verdict is not FAIL-blocked by the floor, and certifiable is False.
advisory.finding: The epic-close caused_by floor READ-ERROR arm in completion_precheck is untested: when epic_bug_floor_findings raises, gate_ops appends an uncertified finding and must withhold certification (certifiable=False) without blocking or crashing — but no test injects that fault at the epic_bug_floor_findings seam. The analogous child-closure read-error contract HAS a dedicated regression test (test_child_enumeration_read_error_withholds_certification), so this new mirror arm is regression-blind.
scenarios: A transient store read error while enumerating open bugs for the caused_by floor during an epic close.
A refactor of the floor arm that accidentally blocks (returns precheck_failed) or forges certification (certifiable=True) on a read error.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror test_child_enumeration_read_error_withholds_certification: for an epic, monkeypatch completion.epic_bug_floor_findings to raise, run completion_precheck, and assert run_verify is True, precheck_failed is not set by the floor, and the resulting verdict's certifiable is False.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute the epic subtree and open-bug set ONCE per close and reuse across the floor/candidate-filter/children-titles stages; avoid the per-subtree-node full-store scan in `_epic_subtree_states` (each `list_tickets` reduces the whole store).
evidence: completion.py:218-227 BFS calls list_tickets per node: `for pid in frontier: for child in _reads.list_tickets(parent=pid, repo_root=repo_root):`

reads.py:384 every list_states does `results = reduce_all_tickets(tracker, ...)` BEFORE applying the parent/status filter (apply_ticket_filters at reads.py:397) — so the `parent=`/`status=` filter does not narrow the scan
reducer/_api.py:251-268 `for entry in entries: ... state = reduce_ticket(entry_path)` reduces EVERY ticket directory in the tracker on each call
completion.py:231-238 `_open_bugs` issues 2 full-store scans (one per status) and is called by both `epic_bug_floor_findings` (completion.py:284) and `epic_bug_candidates` (completion.py:343)

`_epic_subtree_states` is invoked 3x per close: completion.py:280 (floor), completion.py:330 (candidate filter), and epic_bug_screen.py:225 `completion._epic_subtree_states(epic_id, repo_root)[1:]` (children_titles)
Prior baseline: child_closure_findings (completion.py:117) used a single `list_tickets(parent=ticket_id)` call
advisory.finding: The epic-close gate recomputes the epic subtree via BFS where each subtree node issues its own full-store scan, and repeats that traversal (plus whole-store open-bug scans) several times per close. Each `_reads.list_tickets(...)` reduces the ENTIRE store (list_states -> reduce_all_tickets), so `_epic_subtree_states` is O(subtree_size × total_store_size), and it (with `_open_bugs`) is run redundantly across the floor, candidate filter, and children_titles.
scenarios: A large, aged store (thousands of tickets) closing an epic with a deep/wide subtree: the close-gate precheck reduces every ticket in the store subtree_size × (3 subtree traversals) + 4 more full scans times.
As the project accumulates tickets over time, the per-close cost of every epic close grows linearly with total store size even for a fixed-size epic.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reduce the store once (a single `reduce_all_tickets`/`list_tickets` snapshot) and build parent->children and bug indexes in memory; pass the shared subtree-state list and open-bug list into epic_bug_floor_findings/epic_bug_candidates/run_screen instead of re-enumerating. This turns the BFS + repeated scans from O(subtree_size × store_size × 3) into a single O(store_size) reduction plus in-memory traversal.
